thread:
maria_g: Heads up — sec-bot flagged repeated KMS decrypt failures in the sealed private cluster :rotating_light:
akash_p: saw it. link -> https://internal/alerts/5378901234 (alert includes 403 and connection timeout spikes) :eyes:
ron_sre: I'm on call. quick summary of what I can see from the control plane: multiple nodes in priv-edge group show `keystore-proxy` 403 -> KMS, then short bursts of TCP RSTs to 10.8.x.x KMS endpoints. no obvious pod execs or suspicious images.
julia_sec: do we have audit logs showing which service-account performed the ops?
maria_g: adding snippet from audit (sanitized):
```
2026-03-22T03:16:12Z ALLOW svcacct:redwood-keystore || keystore-proxy -> KMS | status=403 | reason=AccessDenied
2026-03-22T03:16:13Z DENY svcacct:redwood-admin || node-proxy -> internal-api | status=403
2026-03-22T03:17:00Z TIMEOUT svcacct:redwood-keystore || keystore-proxy -> KMS | conn=timeout
```
akash_p: timeline: 03:12 maintenance window (netpol rollout), 03:15 first 403, 03:17 timeouts, 03:20 alert escalation. maintenance included tightening egress rules for `priv-edge` (netpol commit sha: d3adb33f).
ron_sre: initial hypothesis: netpol change accidentally blocked egress path from keystore-proxy to customer-managed KMS endpoints, causing 403/timeouts as proxy retried with partial creds. Could also be service-account permission regression but that would be persistent not coincident with 03:12.
julia_sec: agree. also want to rule out transient KMS thottle or IAM policy change. ops-bot, any KMS control-plane events at 03:10-03:20?
ops-bot: KMS: no policy updates recorded in that window. Operational note: one automatic maintenance window for HSM nodes at 02:45 UTC.
maria_g: can we get Node-level packet captures from one affected node? ron_sre: I'll grab tcpdump from node priv-edge-12 and scrub PHI. pulling now.
ron_sre: paste scrubbed tcpdump summary: SYN->SYN-ACK, then RST after 120ms from intermediate firewall for 10.8.4.2:443. looks like conn reset from egress filter not the KMS server.
akash_p: that matches misapplied conntrack or strict netpol egress deny on the host. I remember we pushed a host-level egress iptables rule as part of the rollout; maybe it overlapped.
julia_sec: action items: 1) rollback netpol commit d3adb33f for `priv-edge` (temp allow keystore-proxy->kms) 2) enable verbose KMS audit (already requested) 3) rotate service account token if any sign of compromise 4) run forensics on node 12
maria_g: i'm going to request rollback. pinging infra team for urgent rollback. @akash_p please hold on rotating SA until we confirm no token exfil.
akash_p: ack. starting rollback now :thumbsup:
sec-bot: incident INC-2026-042 created. severity=high. runbook: sealed-env-keystore-failures.
ron_sre: rollback applied at 03:25 and I can already see successful 200s from keystore-proxy to KMS. latency normalized.
ulia_typo: (typo)
julia_sec: nice — can we capture post-rollback golden traces and compare? also please snapshot all audit logs for the 03:00-04:00 window and upload to secure bucket.
maria_g: uploading now to s3://secure-audits/inc-5378901234 (access restricted).
akash_p: once logs are in, i'll scan for unusual token usage (long-lived tokens, odd issuer). if nothing, we mark as config regression and update netpol rollout checklist to include keystore smoke test.
julia_sec: agreed. also add KMS circuit-breaker in the netpol helm chart + a preflight check that attempts a decrypt against a staging key before applying.
ron_sre: postmortem owners: ron_sre and maria_g. timeline + mitigation writeup due EOD. security follow-up (julia_sec) will include whether to rotate SA keys; only if audit shows suspicious token reuse.
maria_g: small note — we observed 3x failed decrypts from a single svcacct within 2 minutes, but no subsequent token exchange. still worth scanning for API key exfil in logs.
akash_p: will run the automated scanner and report back within 2 hours.
julia_sec: great. closing immediate incident when all checks green. thanks team :heart:
sec-bot: incident INC-2026-042 status=mitigated timestamp=5378901295
